However, the app does have some small issues, since the widgets have a weird border, and one time, after completing a quest, I had roughly 1030 XP out of 440 required to level up. This glitch fixed itself after I marked a daily off, and shot me from Level 20 to Level 22.

Overall, keeps me productive, but has some smaller issues that understandably could be a dealbreaker for some.

author: hmklipp

title: Clean interface but lack of updates
body:
I've loved using this app for years and years, and it genuinely helped motivate me to start healthy habits for the better. It's simple but effective, has a clean interface, and the separate tabs for habits/daily tasks/one-off to-dos is so much easier to navigate than other apps that throw them all together in one list. The paid gems & premium subscriptions are pretty reasonable too - free players get full functionality and paid players can buy quests for extra cosmetics or host challenges.

On the downside, the app's had few content updates and once you run out of free quests there's not much left to work towards besides those monetized cosmetics. The community aspect has also wound down - with staff alienating the volunteer mods in a messy situation - so the guilds and chatrooms were shut down too. I learned so much from the supportive communities there, so that social aspect is sorely missed.

TLDR: Good app that could use content updates and a reinvigorated social scene.

(Edited from a previous review)
author: tiredtinker

title: Going downhill
body: I’ve been using Habit off and on since 2014. Its premise is great - get stuff done and meet other people along the way to help motivate you. However, the people in charge now are not the ones who built the app and site. Habit was built by volunteers, but bizarrely, those volunteers have all been shown the door, and now Habit is ending features that got me invested in the app. Two main social hubs, the Tavern and guilds, are being shuttered on August 8th, and with them go two great ways of meeting other people. The app still has a Looking for Group feature, and the Tavern and some of the guilds have migrated to unofficial Discords, but this shutdown of social spaces is not a good sign of things to come.

title: Pleasantly surprised
body: I have ADHD, and a classic trait of ADHD is that while constantly picking up new healthy habits, like keeping a new agenda or setting alarms for tasks etc. is necessary and good, it’s also sort of futile because no matter what, an ADHDer is always going to lapse and drop said habit — which, hey, whatever, just pick it up again and keep trekking on! But it’s still such a discouraging cycle… but Habitica is the first of these new healthy habits I’ve picked up and maintained so easily for such a long stretch of time. It’s genuinely fun! In order to fight monsters and get sick new loot, you HAVE to check into the app, confirm that you’ve done your homework or your chores or you’ve brushed your teeth… what an awesome idea. Oh, and it has tons of “guilds” and “parties” to join which are essentially just fun little clubs focusing on topics from your favourite TV shows to mental health support. The app has minor flaws, sure, and it would be cool if the art and customization features were more elaborate in the future, but Habitica executes this idea decently well and I have nothing to be mad about :)

Second, I like to see my tasks on my phone home screen, but because of the first error the widget only showed the message “Start your day”. I’ve decided to use a similar app, but if these errors are fixed, I shall come back. I like their party/guild system where I can communicate with other ADHD people, and encourage each other.

title: 3 month Review
body:
I’m an Autism/ADHD Support Service Provider and University Student. I’ve been using this daily for 3 months with one of my students (We formed a party).
Here is what it has helped me with:

- Organization
- Positive reinforcement for mundane tasks
- Daily Accountability (And some competitiveness)
- An awesome way to reward my students for assignments that need to be done via “Gems”.
- Reframing schoolwork as “Challenges” instead of..  work.
- Found a fun community (Guild) for people using the Forrest App, which has increased my Forest App usage and productivity tremendously!
- Given me a good way to measure my success as I grind through the first year of a CS degree online. 
- Allowed me to be a kid again.

Here is what it hasn’t helped me with:
- A drive to succeed in life
- It hasn’t magically fixed my problems

All in all, I really enjoy the app and will continue to use it as there is tons to achieve in-game despite being 3 months in. My student and I bond over it, and he actually does homework for gems which is a miracle in itself. The Resource Teacher is impressed, his Mom is stoked, and my student is getting things done. I bought 60 gems for $10 (sale) which I expect to last us both a year in challenges.

Big thanks to the Habitica team for creating such a fun idea and for helping people everywhere get things done. Amazing what some imagination and hard work can do. Cheers.

title: Super fun way to better habits!
body:
Having used this app for a couple years, I can say that my habits are exponentially healthier than they were pre-Habitica. There are also all kinds of ways to interact with other people, if you so chose. Or, you can just do your own thing and be rewarded for your progress (though there are certain aspects of the game that you won’t be able to access alone - like going on quests). I personally feel that some interaction makes for more accountability anyway. Most of the people that I have been sharing a party with are wonderfully supportive, though I have never met them IRL. 

For a few things, the website is much easier to access (Orb of Rebirth, setting pets and mounts free from the stable). But for the most part, these are things that are done more rarely. 

In my time on Habitica, the game has improved a lot and they are always adding new things and fixing any bugs. Shout out to all of those working to always make it better. 

Everything you need to know about how to get the most out of this app is written out in a Fandom Wiki. So, if you are going to really get into it, look for that to find out about all of the great features and how to use them.

body:

I rate it high because other means of motivation and productivity have stopped working as well for me and I was really craving a means of gamifying my life. Also, I didn’t realize how HUGE the Habitica community actually is. There are guilds chock full of resources and chats are always relevant and generally positive, so you can feel good about levelling up alongside others.

Though I do agree that Habitica is best optimized for browser, while on the go there is nothing I love more than having Habitica available on my ipad (browser Habitica on a tablet is not comfortable to use). I decided to give the app another shot after not touching for a number of years. I’m happy I’ve returned to it now.

title: Bugs fixed - Very happy with this app!
body:
I've had an issue for about two weeks on the iPad: I complete my dailies of the night before and in the morning am asked if I want to tick off some that I missed.  A: I hadn't missed any, and B: the tasks the system offers don't apply to the prior day at all, but sometimes to a couple of days on either side.  This morning (Tuesday) it asked if I wanted to mark as complete a habit that only applies to Sundays - and I'm currently "resting" in the tavern...
Looking forward to a bug fix for this.  And, as usual, I thank the programmers & people who work on Habitica - it's an excellent program for me.

Edit: fixed by the next day.  It's all working, and it's all good.  
Original review: The news says that iOS update allows one to choose specific dates for repeating dailies or monthlies, but mine isn't showing that. As well, some of my dailies, which are showing as ticked to repeat today, are - apparently arbitrarily - showing as greyed out when I logged in this morning.  Not sure what's happening in Windows yet (I'll go there next), but for the iPad this update seems glitchy.    I'm sure it'll get fixed - I still love Habitica.

author: Liam Hinzman

title: Changed my life
body:
Finally, a productivity app that's actually motivating!

Habitica's Life-as-an-RPG approach to motivation, combined with the fully flexible structure that lets you customize to YOUR goals and aspirations really worked wonders for the nerd in me! I eyeball different pets and armour sets, and force myself to stick to my resolutions and practice my new habits so I can get that gold and XP so I can buy them! The endless variety of sets makes sure it's not only customizable, but that you'll be hard pressed to collect it all. 

The quests system really ties it all together; after all there's no point in buying a better sword if you've nothing to swing it at! And the social setup is flexible enough that you can play with IRL friends, or make new ones through the app! Very well moderated too so you don't have to worry about chat harassment. 

5/5 would definitely recommend. I love imagining 'Habiteer-Me' getting a power boost from Normal Me's everyday work. Makes normal chores so much more fun!

title: My projects are finally moving forward with this app
body: The app itself is simple, but the concept works wonders. By completing your tasks you earn gold (among other things); I put gold prices to the vacation trip or the "toys" I want to buy... and I see how focusing on the right priorities *pays back* (literally)
author: jorgealfonso

title: Great so far
body: I'm only a couple days into the app, but so far it is working amazingly for me. I laud the group working on this for coming up with and creating a game with such a brilliant concept as Habitica. Five stars from me!
author: Captain Falcon123

title: A widget will be more helpful
body: I really enjoy this idea of RPG my to do items and habits. Still, it is a bit inconvenient to go into app just to tick off tasks or review certain list. A widget in your future update will be really amazing. Thank you for this helpful system and design. Keep up the good work.
author: tpalice

title: Great App
body:
Much better than the old HabitRPG app. Runs much more smoothly and looks better.
The only issue I've come across is far is that the costumes of party members don't show up - only their currently equipped gear.
